findings.source_quote: καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;
findings.english_quote: and indeed, how long shall I prolong the account, unwilling to disclose the painful thing that necessity compels me, even if late, in any event to tell? This same man
findings.issue: The English punctuation leaves the opening construction, ‘Let it be known to you ... that Simon’, without a completed predicate. The Greek brackets the rhetorical interruption and then resumes Simon with οὗτος αὐτός, leading ultimately to his violent death. The draft instead starts a separate sentence whose principal assertion is his proclamation. The claims are present, but their governing syntactic relationship is obscured. The printed high point is an editorial feature, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Bracket the entire rhetorical interruption with paired dashes or parentheses, then resume and complete the original ‘that Simon’ construction. Keep the proclamation subordinate, for example with ‘having ... proclaimed’, and carry the sentence through his departure from life. Retain the disclosed uncertainty about the rhetorical question’s scope. The revised sentence requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς
findings.english_quote: so that whatever he determines on earth will stand decreed in the heavens
findings.issue: The main rendering suppresses περὶ, ‘concerning’, and conceals the recurrence of χειροτονέω, rendered earlier as ‘ordain’. The Greek frames the heavenly decree as concerning the person or matter affected by Clement’s action; the English directly identifies whatever he determines with what stands decreed. The notes correctly disclose the possible personal referent, but that disclosure does not restore the wording relationship in the main text. Neither the personal nor the impersonal interpretation should be certified as uniquely established.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore ‘concerning’ and explicitly compare a source-transparent rendering such as ‘so that concerning whatever he ordains on earth, it will stand decreed in the heavens’ with the personal alternative ‘so that concerning anyone he appoints on earth, it will stand decreed in the heavens’. Preserve the alternative interpretation in the notes and maintain a visible connection with the earlier χειροτονῶ. These are provisional candidates requiring fresh review, not accepted replacements.

findings.source_quote: καὶ σὲ δὲ περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν ἐὰν μὴ νοῶσιν, παρὰ τῶν διακόνων μανθανέτωσαν
findings.english_quote: Moreover, if they all do not understand that they must keep you free from concern about the matters from which you must be free, let them learn it from the deacons
findings.issue: ‘The matters from which you must be free’ changes freedom from concern about those matters into freedom from the matters themselves. The Greek has περὶ ὧν with ἀμέριμνον εἶναι: being without care concerning them. The draft also expresses two separate ‘must’ relationships where the marked Greek construction contains one χρὴ. Its attachment to εἶναι and its relationship to ποιεῖν deserve disclosure rather than silent expansion. This is a syntactic and interpretive question, not evidence of an OCR error or missing text.
findings.suggested_revision: Recast the sentence so that the freedom is explicitly freedom from concern about the matters. Compare the provisional candidate ‘Moreover, if they all do not understand about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern, let them learn from the deacons.’ In source_issues, disclose whether χρὴ is understood as governing their making you free from concern or your being free from concern; do not posit a Greek correction merely because the word order is marked. Review the revised wording afresh.
